title: Planning a TypeScript Project knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the strongest evidence that an application design is ready for review?
options: A successful compile with no runtime checks or acceptance criteria.
Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
A large number of abstractions without tests.
Only a screenshot of the happy path.
questions.answer_key: Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
questions.explanation: Production-oriented work is supported by explicit acceptance criteria and repeatable evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Planning a TypeScript Project”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with requirements and user stories and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with requirements and user stories and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Requirements and user stories”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Planning a TypeScript Project”?
options: Assume architecture and module boundaries is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check data and error models, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check data and error models, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Data and error models”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
